review.crlfIndependence: Every incorrect source was re-run on LF-normalized copies of all test inputs; first failing test unchanged and numerically wrong answers persist, so no counterexample depends on CRLF line endings.
review.incorrectAreAlgorithmic: Every incorrect source read in full; each prints a numerically wrong answer on valid tests (format/debug-only failures not counted).
review.independentOracle: Minimum over all orders of the six pieces (four a, two b) of next-fit bar packing; cross-checked against exhaustive assignment of pieces to up to six bars for 300 random small inputs.
review.officialTests: official_tests_complete=true, testset_size 120; package tests 0001-0120 equal the pinned row's official tests positionally (CRLF-normalized inputs, token-equal outputs); source row equals the sha-verified pinned parquet row.
review.oracleResult: All 274 package tests and all samples pass a strict format/range parse; every expected output equals my oracle; all upstream official rows equal my oracle.
review.sandbox: Own harness (sha256 c582ff42...983d0d; not worker pool_harness): pinned python@sha256:5887f265...05d3, --network=none, --read-only, --user=65534, --cap-drop=ALL, no-new-privileges, pids<=32, 1 CPU, 2560m memory, RLIMIT_CPU/AS at problem limits, bounded output, launched from env -i shell without credentials; g++ -O2 -std=c++17 -DONLINE_JUDGE.
review.singleAnswer: Output is uniquely determined by the input; token comparison is correct; no special checker or float tolerance.
review.statement: Bounds '1 ≤ n ≤ 1 000', '1 ≤ a ≤ n', '1 ≤ b ≤ n' are written in full; no exponent markup. Input is three lines with one integer each; all 274 tests and 4 samples now use exactly that layout (154 worker-authored tests 0121-0274 regenerated; values equal the previous one-line versions token for token).
review.submissionProvenance: All sources byte-identical (sha256) to rows in pinned open-r1/codeforces-submissions shards (shard sha256 verified independently); upstream verdict/problem/language match; for every incorrect source the first failing package test equals upstream passedTestCount+1.

submissions.defect: packing loop is bounded by i+1<n instead of i+1<6, so for n<6 it cannot merge pieces; on 3 1 2 (test 0006) it prints 4, expected 3. Output identical at -O0, -O2 and a repeat run
greedy largest-first packing with an early 'n >= 2*(2a+b)' shortcut; not optimal (first wrong at 0082)

first-fit in fixed order a,a,a,a,b,b is not optimal; on 1000 1 998 (test 0012) it prints 3, expected 2. The in-bounds algorithm alone is wrong on the same 28 tests; the c[6] read in its count loop does not change any output (identical at -O0 and -O2)
fills the current bar with the first piece that fits, in fixed order, which is not optimal; same 28 wrong tests, first 0012
simulates one fixed order a,a,b,a,a,b and discards leftover space when the next piece does not fit; on 800 401 400 (test 0016) it prints 6, expected 5
